subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by the shared fenced reply-session self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920, or should webchat and heartbeat keep explicit retry or spool handling even after that shared fix?
rationale: The evidence supports both the shared root-cause fix and surface-specific preservation concerns; choosing the permanent owner boundary changes session lifecycle behavior and channel retry policy.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest webchat and heartbeat conflict cases before adding surface-specific retry loops.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep this issue open for a separate webchat and heartbeat retry/spool repair even if the shared self-heal lands.

options.title: Ask For Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request current-main live reproduction for the exact webchat or heartbeat path before choosing the repair layer.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest webchat and heartbeat conflict cases before adding surface-specific retry loops.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has recent merged history on the guarded reply-session initialization boundary where the owner-boundary decision sits.
